body.statement: For \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with uniform \(q\), \(F_{\mathcal J}=107/72\) and \(F_{\mathcal J,2}=F_{\mathcal J,3}=55/36\), so the exact gap is \(1/24\). By the strict class-inclusion proposition, every quadratic candidate allowed by the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje framework lies in the Boolean comparison class \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\); hence the same \(55/36\) lower certificate rules out every such published candidate, although it does not assert that \(55/36\) is the optimum of their smaller positive-semidefinite class. The displayed bounds satisfy \(r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)=[1+x_0x_1x_2x_5]/24\in\{0,1/12\}\), and \(b^\star(\theta)=3^{-1}\sum_{z=1}^3h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})\) with every table entry in \([0,5]\). The distribution \(\mu^\star\) certifies \(107/72\), and \(\nu^\star\) certifies \(55/36\), by exact observable-margin equalities and complementary slackness across all sixty-four schedules.
body.proof_tex:
All finite calculations below are over \(\mathbb Q\).  The score vectors in \(\mathfrak E_\star\) have supports contained in their respective observation sets.  Substitution in \(\text{def:score-variance}\) gives
\[
c=\left(-\frac23,-1,\frac23,0,-\frac13,\frac43\right)
\]
and
\[
9A=
\begin{pmatrix}
8&0&-8&0&-2&2\\
0&6&0&6&-3&-9\\
-8&0&8&0&2&-2\\
0&6&0&6&-3&-9\\
-2&-3&2&-3&2&4\\
2&-9&-2&-9&4&14
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{16}
\]
The observable complex consists of the empty set, the six singletons, the nine pairs
\[
01,02,05,12,13,15,25,34,35,
\]
the five triples \(012,015,025,125,135\), and the quartet \(0125\).  Here a digit string denotes the corresponding subset of \(I\).

Boolean inversion of the displayed formula for \(b^\star\), independently recomputed from the three lexicographically ordered assignment tables, gives the following complete list of nonzero coefficients (every unlisted coefficient, including \(\beta_\varnothing\), is zero).  In particular, the two singleton checks are
\[
 \beta_{\{4\}}=\frac{h_2^\star(01)-h_2^\star(00)}3=\frac13,
 \qquad
 \beta_{\{5\}}=\frac{h_1^\star(001)-h_1^\star(000)+h_3^\star(0001)-h_3^\star(0000)}3=\frac73,
\]
so the table is tied directly to both the displayed formula and the implementation certificate:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr}
S&0&1&2&3&4&5&02&12&13\\ \hline
\beta_S&8/9&2/3&11/9&2/3&1/3&7/3&-19/9&-1/3&4/3
\end{array}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr}
S&15&25&34&35&012&015&025&125&0125\\ \hline
\beta_S&-8/3&-1/3&-2/3&-2&1/3&1/3&1/3&1/3&-2/3.
\end{array} \tag{17}
\]
Every listed support belongs to \(\mathcal J\), so \(b^\star\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}\).  Since \(\beta_{0125}=-2/3\ne0\), uniqueness of Boolean inversion also gives \(b^\star\notin\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\).  The formula for \(r^\star\) contains only a constant and the nine displayed observable pairs in centered coordinates.  Expanding \(x_i x_k=(2\theta_i-1)(2\theta_k-1)\) therefore proves \(r^\star\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\).

We next check all domination constraints exactly.  Order \(\Theta\) lexicographically as \(000000,000001,\ldots,111111\).  Substitution of (16) into \(f(\theta)=\theta^\top A\theta\) and subtraction from the formula for \(b^\star\) gives
\[
72\{b^\star-f\}=
\begin{array}{rrrrrrrr}
0&56&8&0&0&56&8&0\\
24&88&0&0&24&88&0&0\\
0&8&56&0&0&8&56&0\\
0&40&24&0&0&40&24&0\\
0&24&40&0&0&24&40&0\\
0&56&8&0&0&56&8&0\\
0&0&88&24&0&0&88&24\\
0&8&56&0&0&8&56&0.
\end{array} \tag{18}
\]
Every entry is nonnegative, so \(b^\star\ge f\) on all sixty-four schedules.  If \(w(\theta):=x_0x_1x_2x_5\in\{-1,1\}\), then direct subtraction gives
\[
r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)
=\frac{110-107+3w(\theta)}{72}
=\frac{1+w(\theta)}{24}\in\left\{0,\frac1{12}\right\}. \tag{19}
\]
Thus \(r^\star\ge b^\star\ge f\).  Under uniform \(q\), every nonconstant centered monomial has mean zero, and hence
\[
\mathbb E_q b^\star=\frac{107}{72},
\qquad
\mathbb E_q r^\star=\frac{110}{72}=\frac{55}{36}. \tag{20}
\]

The assignment-level certificate is also exact.  Let \(\iota_z(\theta)\) be the lexicographic index of \(\theta|_{O_z}\).  Expanding the three displayed tables and applying Boolean inversion gives exactly the coefficient list (17), so
\[
b^\star(\theta)=\frac13\sum_{z=1}^3
h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})
\qquad(\theta\in\Theta). \tag{21}
\]
This verifies all sixty-four implementation equalities without approximation.  Inspection of the twenty-eight displayed table entries gives
\[
0\le h_z^\star(y)\le5
\qquad
(z=1,2,3;\ y\in\{0,1\}^{O_z}). \tag{22}
\]

For the all-degree lower certificate, each of the eight \(O_1\)-patterns occurs twice in the sixteen-point support of \(\mu^\star\), each of the four \(O_2\)-patterns occurs four times, and each of the sixteen \(O_3\)-patterns occurs once.  Thus \(\mu^\star\) has the same marginal as uniform \(q\) on every displayed observation set, and therefore matches every moment \(m_S\) for \(S\in\mathcal J\).  Hence \(\mu^\star\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal J}(q)\).  The values of \(f\) on its support, in the order of \(\text{def:witness-experiment}\), are
\[
0,\frac23,\frac{32}{9},\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac83,
\frac{32}{9},\frac89,\frac89,\frac{14}{9},\frac83,\frac23,
\frac{14}{9},\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac23. \tag{23}
\]
Their mean is \(107/72\).  The entries of (18) at all sixteen support schedules are zero, so complementary slackness holds.  The dual equality in \(\text{thm:dual-complete-class}\), together with (20), yields
\[
F_{\mathcal J}=\frac{107}{72}. \tag{24}
\]

For the degree-three program, the eight-point support of \(\nu^\star\) contains every \(O_1\)-pattern once and every \(O_2\)-pattern twice.  Its \(O_3\)-projections are the eight odd-parity four-bit strings.  If at most three of those four bits are fixed, there are exactly \(2^{3-|S|}\) odd-parity completions; consequently each proper-subset \(S\subsetneq O_3\) has the uniform moment \(2^{-|S|}\).  Therefore \(\nu^\star\) matches uniform \(q\) on every observable monomial of degree at most three.  Its corresponding variance values are
\[
\frac83,\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac89,
\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac{14}{9},\frac83, \tag{25}
\]
whose mean is \(55/36\); direct substitution also gives \(r^\star=f\) at these eight schedules.  For any \(b\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\), moment matching and pointwise domination imply
\[
\mathbb E_qb=\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}b
\ge\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}f=\frac{55}{36}. \tag{26}
\]
Feasibility of \(r^\star\), the nesting \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\), and (26) give
\[
\frac{55}{36}\le F_{\mathcal J,3}
\le F_{\mathcal J,2}\le\frac{55}{36}. \tag{27}
\]
Thus \(F_{\mathcal J,2}=F_{\mathcal J,3}=55/36\).  The one missing observable moment is the quartet:
\[
\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}m_{0125}=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_qm_{0125}=\frac1{16},
\]
or, in centered coordinates, \(\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}x_0x_1x_2x_5=-1\) while the uniform expectation is zero.  Equations (24) and (27) prove the exact Boolean gap
\[
\frac{55}{36}-\frac{107}{72}=\frac1{24}. \tag{28}
\]
They also show why degree four is the first possible improvement: \(A\mathbf 1_6=0\) follows from (16), uniform \(q\) is complement invariant, and \(\text{thm:complement-degree-collapse}\) therefore gives equality of the degree-two and degree-three optima; the observable quartet in (17) then supplies the first available even degree beyond two.

Finally, every witness coordinate is observed with positive probability, so \(\text{prop:hms-class-inclusion}\) places each compatible conservative Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic in the Boolean degree-two feasible class.  Equation (27) therefore gives the valid enlarged-class lower bound \(55/36\) for every such quadratic.  The exact semidefinite certificate in \(\text{prop:witness-hms-sdp-optimum}\) strengthens this comparison by solving the smaller published class itself:
\[
\min_H\mathbb E_q h_H=\frac76+\frac{\sqrt{17}}9,
\qquad
\left(\frac76+\frac{\sqrt{17}}9\right)-\frac{107}{72}
=\frac{8\sqrt{17}-23}{72}. \tag{29}
\]
This direct Harshaw--Middleton--Savje gap is approximately \(0.138678403\), whereas (28) remains the stronger class statement against every observable Boolean quadratic or cubic rule.
body.justification: The exact certificates distinguish the all-observable quartic optimum, the larger Boolean quadratic/cubic optimum, and the smaller published positive-semidefinite quadratic optimum.
body.gap: Neither \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} nor \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} contains this quartic witness, the \(1/24\) Boolean degree gap, or the exact \((8\sqrt{17}-23)/72\) direct quadratic-class gap.
body.consumer: It supplies a reproducible rational truth-table test and an exact algebraic semidefinite benchmark without equating the two quadratic comparison classes.
